question: With chromatin gating, a compiled run predicts a gene's element-driven contribution ON only in the reader cell types whose reader states the element open. Across the thirteen reader cell types, does that gated prediction track measured RNA better than a no-rule baseline, and better than the ungated run as compiled (the rule on in its compiled cell only)?

structure.identifiable: the bridge fits one strength per mechanism and refuses a gene regulated by more than one in a cell (not_identifiable). Under SELECTION_READER_CELLS every predicted rule of a gene is offered in every reader cell, so a gene is runnable only if exactly ONE regulatory rule targets it over all 24 programs; a gene with several elements has no fitted parameters to run
structure.two_levels: for such a gene the gated run has two levels: L_open, where the cell's reader states the element open and the rule runs, and L_held, where it is closed or unknown and the rule is held at strength 0 (for one activating rule the basal rate; for one inhibiting rule basal + max_rate). m = log2(L_open / L_held) equals the observation's -log2(RHO) and does not depend on the borrowed rate, the Hill parameters or the mRNA half-life (runrules.READING)
structure.offered_everywhere: a run that offers the rule in every reader cell WITHOUT a reader runs it everywhere: one level in all thirteen cells, which after centring within the gene predicts no difference between cells. Under the registered endpoint it is the no-rule baseline exactly, so it is not a separate test
structure.network: no compiled rule's source is a gene (runrules census): one independent system per gene
structure.bridge_drops_through: bridge.parameterize rebuilds each fitted rule without `through`, so a bridged program runs ungated unless `through` is put back; run_gene puts it back and checks the gated level against the clamped level of the cell's state at every gene and cell

money: none: no request is sent and no key is read
reading: worse: the reader-gated run raised the squared error of measured log2(TPM+1) across the thirteen reader cell types above the no-rule baseline's (Delta MSE -0.06154 [95% CI -0.08665, -0.03963] over 6,773 gene-cell pairs, 521 genes; control p = 0.00799) and was further from measured RNA than the ungated run as compiled (MSE difference -0.05389 [95% CI -0.0753, -0.03508])
limitations: independence: each rule's sign and size m come from AlphaGenome's RNA-seq gene scorer (an in-silico deletion, the argmax over 371 RNA-seq tracks), a model trained on ENCODE and GTEx RNA-seq, with RNA-seq tracks named for the reader biosamples among them, and on ENCODE DNase-seq; the reader's open/closed calls are ENCODE DNase-seq narrowPeak files, a measurement of the same biosamples; the measured outcome is ENCODE polyA plus RNA-seq of those biosamples, data of the kind, and possibly the very experiments, the model was trained on. The cross-cell pattern of the gated prediction comes from the DNase calls alone and its sign and size from the model

accessibility near a gene tracks its expression across cell types whatever any compiled rule says, so a gated run that beats the baseline may carry only that association; the shuffled-reader control and the unsigned-openness descriptive bound how much of a gain belongs to the gene's own element and to the rule's sign. An open element is one a rule may act through, not evidence that it does; no reading here is evidence of a mechanism

the population is the genes with exactly one compiled rule over the genome, a small and selected subset of the genes with any rule: a gene with several elements is not identifiable under the bridge and is not run
m transports the AlphaGenome effect of the rule's compiled cell (the track where the deletion moved the gene most) to every reader cell where the element is open

one polyA plus experiment per biosample, from several labs; two of the thirteen are tissues (ovary, testis) and the rest cell lines or primary or derived cells. Every rate under the run is mouse NIH 3T3 or their genome median; m does not depend on it and no level in molecules per cell is quoted

ungated_as_compiled.clause: further from measured RNA than the ungated run as compiled

entry_script.why: argv[0] is a file inside this repository that git tracks and reports unmodified: the commit holds the code that wrote the bytes, so a rebuild can run it. The only clean form
entry_script.forms_are_decided_in_advance: genomeos.manifest.ENTRY_FORMS: one clean form (a tracked, unmodified file inside this repository), every other form refuses, and a form that cannot be classified is 'unknown' and refuses too. Read from sys.argv[0] at write time, never declared

code_cleanliness.counting_path_is_computed: the transitive import closure of this script, computed from the files' import statements at write time (genomeos.manifest.counting_path), never by importing: it follows every import that resolves to a file in this repository rather than only the package, counts the __init__.py of each package above a module, resolves bare imports against the directories the source literally puts on sys.path as well as the repository root, and matches every path component against what its directory lists, so a class name such as genomeos.genome.Genome cannot enter it as a file; not a hand-written list
code_cleanliness.note: several lanes work in this one checkout. A file under foreign_uncommitted_code belongs to another lane; this lane did not write it and did not commit it. The counting path is the computed closure above, so a foreign file outside it cannot have entered a number here, and foreign_uncommitted_code_on_the_counting_path names any that could

revision_stamps.sampled: code_cleanliness.git_sha is read while the writer computes; code.git_sha is read when the result is written. Both are HEAD of the same checkout at two moments
revision_stamps.reading: no revision race: both stamps record 9293190

traced_inputs.note: Every file this writer opened for reading under data/ was recorded by an audit hook on the "open" event, canonicalised through data/'s links so one file has one spelling, and compared against the inputs the manifest declares; a member of a declared group counts as declared and hashed on its own, a file under a declared directory counts as declared by prefix. The hook is per interpreter, so a file read by a subprocess is not in this record, nor is one reached through a path that canonicalises to neither this checkout's data/ nor one of its link targets.
